messages:
amy: quick heads-up — running a short interruption surge exercise tomorrow to validate mixed-capacity behavior (A100 + T4 pool). target: 40% spot interruptions across the inference fleet for 10m. objective: ensure graceful routing, cache recovery, and cost signals are intact. :rocket:

mike: SGTM. what time? and which regions?

amy: 11:00 UTC, start in us-west1-c then us-east4-b if all looks good. keeping dedicated capacity baseline at 20% to avoid total outage.

jordan: can we test the routing policy that falls back to lower-cost model variants under capacity pressure? want to validate the metric tagging for those requests.

amy: yep — will enable canary routing to 'redwood-mini-v2' for 10% of traffic when node pressure > 60%. also will add a header X-RW-FALLBACK so downstream can track.

sara: add abort conditions in the runbook: p95 latency > 200ms for 5m OR error rate > 3% for 3m -> stop simulation and roll back routing. also notify oncall.

amy: runbook snippet we will follow:
```
- 10:45: confirm runbook & alerts
- 10:50: throttle non-prod traffic to 30%
- 11:00: invoke spot-terminate script with --pct=40 --zones=us-west1-c
- 11:02: watch p95, err%, kv-cache-hit
- 11:10: scale review & inject routing fallback if needed
- 11:15: end simulation, collect traces
```

mike: what's the script? can we do a dry run first?

amy: script (dry-run mode):
```
./tools/simulate_preemptions.sh --label=inference-pool --pct=40 --dry-run
```
It lists nodes that would be impacted. actual run will hit the cloud provider API to preempt VMs.

jordan: important: include mixed GPU distribution check. if A100 nodes get hit disproportionately, autoscaler may be slow to provision T4s -> we want to ensure kernel selection fallback works. add a step to validate model-quantized routes.

amy: noted. will run a quick health check after triggers: `./tools/check_kernel_fallbacks.sh` and verify model variance metrics.

ops-bot: scheduled: interruption-surge exec queued by amy for 1768003600 (epoch). notify: oncall@sre in 15m.

sara: tagging cost folks: we need post-run cost delta for spot vs reserved shift. expectation: short-term burst uses dedicated fallback which increases short billing; capture that.

mike: after-action items:
- collect per-route token cost delta (amy)
- verify cache warm-up times and prefix hit rates (jordan)
- capture pod restart counts and node replacement latency (sara)

amy: will capture traces and synthetic evals. plan to run 1k synthetic requests per route pre/post.

mike: during simulation: watch cluster events (`kubectl get events -w`) and autoscaler metrics. if autoscaler lags > 3m, abort.

amy: postmortem success criteria:
- latency degradation p95 <= +40ms and recovers within 3m of end
- error rate under abort thresholds (<=3%)
- KV/prefix cache hit recovers to >= 90% of baseline within 5m
- no user-facing 5xx spike in production routes

jordan: small ask — add a sigterm handling test for the runtime to ensure KV cache is persisted/fallback works before termination. we've seen cold-starts blow costs.

amy: good call. adding a 30s drain window test and validating warm-start path.

ops-bot: simulation results (summary): terminated 14 spot nodes in us-west1-c, autoscaler added 9 dedicated nodes, p95 +32ms, errors peaked at 1.8%, KV hit dropped to 62% during the surge and recovered to 93% within 4m. traces uploaded to /runs/1768000000/summaries.

sara: that looks within success criteria — KV recovery is slightly faster than our threshold. cost team: please analyze billing for the 15m window, include pre/post reserved use.

mike: good job. next steps: tighten routing fallback window to 30s and automate abort if p95 > 180ms. also schedule a longer 30m run in a staging env.

amy: ack. I'll update the runbook and post the artifacts. thanks all :thumbsup:
